decisions.rationale: Verified against all collections-streams topic.json files: of 42 taught objectives (excluding the review-scenarios page), the blueprint lists 36; section 5 names only generics#o1, stacks-and-queues#o3 and timed-coding-screen-patterns#o2, omitting choosing-the-right-collection#o2, the-equals-and-hashcode-contract#o1 and wrapper-types-and-autoboxing#o1. Topic-level coverage holds. Fix must achieve: section 5 lists all six untargeted objectives with honest reasons. Prefer listing over folding them into q05/q07/q09, because folding raises objectives per item and works against the time-fit constraints accepted under education-2; if any is folded, add it to blueprint objectives and objectiveFormats consistently. Same fix closes sme-b4.

Verified line 133: the plan flags that harder applied items at 60 s each fit only with short snippets but leaves the decision to the private author, and q13/q15 carry 3-4 objectives each. The 15 items / 15 minutes / pass mark 70 and the separate coding practical are fixed by the course owner, so the 12-item fallback and moving practical minutes are not author options. Fix must achieve: the coverage plan records binding value-free authoring constraints that make 15 items in 15 minutes credible (snippet length cap of about 8 lines, at most two objectives per item, q13 and q15 reduced to one decision each), requires pilot timing of each item recorded as 'timed at <commit>' without values, and replaces the fallback options with an explicit statement that if pilot timing fails the fit problem goes to the course owner for decision; blueprint itemCounts, durationMinutes and passMark stay unchanged.

Verified: objectiveFormats credits three or four objectives to single four-option items q09, q12, q13, q14, q15; one keyed response cannot evidence all of them, so objective-level reporting would overstate mastery. Fix must achieve: the section 4 table names one primary objective per planned item and lists any others as context, and every taught topic keeps at least one item where one of its objectives is primary; this also supports the at-most-two-objectives constraint from education-2.

Verified: section 4 asserts 'new and harder' but records no per-item cognitive level, no single- vs cross-topic marker and no ordering principle (items follow syllabus order), so the step-up claim is not reviewable. Fix must achieve: a value-free column per item for cognitive level (apply/analyze/evaluate) and single- or cross-topic, plus a stated intended order; no stems, options or keys added.

Verified line 167 and allowedResources[0]: the instructions are one long paragraph using internal calendar labels ('Day F28', 'F28 module check') and say both 'the course's one graded, cumulative multiple-choice assessment' and 'part of the module check'; allowedResources[0] is author-facing ('The frozen calendar states no AI or resource rule...'). Fix must achieve: short learner-facing instructions without calendar ids that still state the fixed facts (graded final quiz ending Course Review, 15 questions in 15 minutes covering every topic, question types, coding practical is separate, pass mark 70%, resource rules shown by the platform), and learner-facing allowedResources wording; passMark, itemCounts and durationMinutes unchanged.

Verified: q09 ('choose an implementation for several stated needs at once') has the same shape as review-scenarios Activity 1; q05 (counting map failing on an unseen key) sits close to the wrapper-types GIFT 'unboxing null' item (prices.get("tea") into double) and to collections-module-check coding Task 1 ('count values with merge or getOrDefault'); q10/q14 mirror coding Task 2 ('sort ... by two keys with a Comparator, then group ... where keys can repeat'). Section 6's generic list leaves these known collisions for the private author to discover. Fix must achieve: section 6 names these collisions explicitly and constrains q09 to a different decision dimension (e.g. cost versus order conflict) and q05, q10, q14 to not preview the coding practical's tasks, all value-free.

Technically correct per the Java SE 25 Stream API: count() may skip executing the pipeline when the count is computable from the source, so peek/map side effects before count() are not reliable output; stream reuse 'may' throw IllegalStateException with an implementation-defined message. An item keyed on either would be unverifiable. Fix must achieve: a value-free authoring constraint for q13 in the coverage plan: demonstrate laziness only with a terminal operation that must traverse elements (never peek/map + count()), key reuse on the exception type not its message, and verify keyed behavior on a JDK 25 run recorded without values.

Technically correct: ConcurrentModificationException is best-effort (removing the second-to-last element in a for-each over an ArrayList completes without throwing); List.of/Set.of/Map.of reject modification and nulls; ArrayDeque rejects null elements, which is what makes poll/peek returning null on empty unambiguous. These are known item-keying traps for q02 and q03. Fix must achieve: value-free authoring constraints in the coverage plan for q02 (avoid the second-to-last removal case, or make the cause UnsupportedOperationException from List.of) and q03 (no null insertion; throwing vs null-returning empty-deque methods keyed per the Deque API).

Technically correct: HashMap/HashSet iteration order and bucket-index computation are unspecified by the API, and Comparator.comparing(key) throws NullPointerException on null keys unless wrapped with nullsFirst/nullsLast, while reversed() reverses the whole comparator composed so far. Items q01, q08 and q10 could otherwise key unverifiable or wrong outputs. Fix must achieve: value-free authoring constraints: q01/q08 key Hash* results on contents and size only (order only for LinkedHash*/Tree*), q08 at the documented hashCode-selects-bucket / equals-finds-entry level with no numeric bucket index, q10 places reversed() deliberately and handles nulls with nullsFirst/nullsLast, with keyed order verified on a JDK 25 run recorded without values.

Same verified gap as education-1: choosing-the-right-collection#o2, the-equals-and-hashcode-contract#o1 and wrapper-types-and-autoboxing#o1 are absent from the blueprint yet unlisted in section 5; all 36 listed references resolve and objectiveFormats matches objectives exactly. Fix must achieve what education-1 specifies: all six omissions listed with honest reasons (preferred), or any folded objective added consistently to blueprint objectives, objectiveFormats and the section 4 row.

Verified on 26d42402: the instructions say 'Later questions combine two topics', but the coverage plan's delivery-order table marks q11, q12 and q13 single-topic and cross-topic items at q02, q07, q10, q14, q15, and the plan claims only that cross-topic items 'appear more often towards the end'. Fix must achieve: learner-facing wording no stronger than the plan (e.g. 'Some questions, more often the later ones, combine two topics'), with itemCounts, durationMinutes and passMark unchanged. Related observation for the same correction: q15 is labelled cross-topic while its primary and secondary objectives both belong to timed-coding-screen-patterns; the author should make that scope label consistent with its objectives so the plan supports the reworded sentence.
